stories.title: Bitcoin stays just under $60,000 as Asian chip stocks slide and bitcoin funds keep losing money
stories.summary: Bitcoin stayed just under $60,000 in Asian trading on Wednesday as chip stocks fell hard in Seoul and Tokyo, after US technology shares gave back ground on Tuesday. US spot bitcoin funds have lost money five days in a row and are having their worst month on record.
points: Bitcoin was about $59,850, down 2.3% over 24 hours, at about 03:10 UTC Wednesday, per Why It Moved.
South Korea's Kospi fell nearly 6% and Japan's Nikkei more than 3% as doubts about AI returned, per investingLive.
US spot bitcoin funds lost $569.7 million on Monday 23 Nov, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $509.3 million, per The Block.
Bitcoin funds have lost about $4.71 billion in November so far, the most for any month since they launched, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Official fund-flow figures for Tuesday 24 Nov were not yet available when this was written.

stories.title: Today's US inflation report is the last big one before the Fed's December decision
stories.summary: October's PCE inflation report, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, comes out today at 8:30am ET (20:30 Bangkok), with a revised Q3 growth figure and weekly jobless claims. Traders expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates on 9 December. Higher rates tend to weigh on risky assets like crypto, so prices can swing right after the release.
points: Headline PCE prices are expected to rise 3.8% on the year, up from 3.6% in September, per investingLive.
Core PCE, which leaves out food and energy, is expected at about 3.2% on the year, up from 3.1%, per investingLive.
Markets price about a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike on 9 Dec, from the current 3.75-4.00% range, per investingLive.
The Fed's decision is Wed 9 Dec at 2:00pm ET (02:00 Thu Bangkok), per the Federal Reserve.

stories.title: New US tariffs on 16 trading partners still expected, not yet announced
stories.summary: The US Trade Representative is expected to publish the results of its investigation into "structural excess capacity" in 16 economies "in the coming days", followed by new import taxes, according to AP's sources. Nothing had been announced as of the latest reports. Tariffs can push prices up, which makes rate hikes more likely, and bitcoin has been moving with stocks.
points: The 16 economies include China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, India, Mexico, Vietnam and Taiwan, per USTR's March announcement of the investigation.
AP reported on the evening of 24 Nov that results were expected "in the coming days" and that timing could still change, per ClickOnDetroit.
Countries with recent trade deals, such as the EU, Japan and South Korea at 15%, would likely keep those rates, per Dimerco, which says final rates are unclear.
The new duties would replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February, per AP.

briefs.title: SEC staff gives Molecule no-action relief
briefs.summary: The SEC's Corporation Finance staff said it will not recommend enforcement over Molecule's science-research project tokens, adding to recent no-action letters for DoubleZero, Fuse and Canton, per The Block.

briefs.title: $2.57 million drained from trader Ansem's wallet
briefs.summary: A suspected attacker moved $2.57 million in USDC out of memecoin trader Ansem's wallet and his Black Bull coin fell 55%; Ansem denies involvement, per The Block.

briefs.title: Monad (MON) had a big unlock scheduled for 24 Nov
briefs.summary: About 16.61 billion MON, roughly 32% of its released supply, was scheduled to unlock on 24 Nov, per KuCoin.

briefs.title: French Senate rejects crypto tax changes
briefs.summary: The French Senate rejected amendments that would have required reporting of self-held crypto worth at least €100,000, added an exit tax on crypto and taxed crypto-to-stablecoin swaps, per KuCoin.

briefs.title: South Korea drafts a new digital-asset law
briefs.summary: A draft law would allow ICOs, set up a bank-centred framework for local-currency stablecoins and cap major shareholders of exchanges at 20%, per KuCoin's daily report.
